Today I am going to present an idea to categorize the behaviors of certain groups of people. Among these groups are modern feminists in developed nations, like America, Sweden, and the UK. Other groups like Social Justice Warriors, and their relation to activities of groups like GamerGate, are also relevant due to their being an exclusively modern phenomenon. I will endeavor to be brief, as I'm certain nobody wants to listen to a nobody talk for 30 minutes about excruiating details. Therefore, if I gloss over whole swaths of detail, I am doing so to endeavor to present a simpler, briefer idea, and not out of ignorance. Please be patient as I experiment with this format.

What I will argue is that these groups of people embody, like charicatures, the ideals put forth by romance-era literature, art, and philosophy. As I've brought this up in discussions and found myself criticized for daring to suppose they're as great in mind as romance era people, I must clarify they are only EMBODYING the emergent CONSEQUENCES of these ideals. This, and only this, is why I label them "NeoRomantics".

Elements of romantic thought came from fictional literature and art, often depicting emphasis on the emotional or irrational. In general you would find depictions of the sublime experience of children, love, nature, and other wonderment inducing states of being. The consequences of these states of being, however, are often also depicted in the same works. Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, who wrote "The Sorrows of Young Werthe" which characterizes this attitude with the protagonist Werther. Goethe directs our sympathy to admire Wether who later kills himself, unable to fulfill his desire for love in the class he was born into. Romantics often portrayed the consequences of their ideals, not as argument against the ideal, but as argument against the adult-minded intellectual or industrial focused world of the era.

What concerns us is not the appeals to nature that romantics often portrayed, such as the works of William Wordsworth, but the ideals of irrationality and creativity more in line with the consequences of works like "The sleep of reason" by Francisco Goya in 1798. It is the depictions of emotion, and subtle anti-intellectual undertones of such works, which drives my parallel. Such depictions of reason in opposition to creativity, or that creativity exists only in the chaos of emotion, is still held in modern minds. Although emotionally driven creativity, without reason, can be nothing but meaningless noise like splattering paint on a canvas. For the consequence of idealizing this childlike creative irrationality is what we are seeing embodied in the modern age.

Also relevant is the childlike or more natural idealization of humanity, which we would later see romantics portray regarding native americans. Appealing to the masses that humanity is most comfortable "in tune with nature", or that humanity has fallen prey to the cynicism and cruelty of reason against this natural state. What we see in the modern era, what I call NeoRomanticism, is the consequential embodiment of adopting these ideals.

I wish to give some examples to characterize what I see as this embodiment. Neoromantics will argue, for example, that all views are equally valid, and by arguing something is invalid you are being oppressive. As NeoRomantics embody an emotion centric life, any disagreements that propose them to be wrong will make them feel bad. This results in the creation of so-called "safe spaces", takedowns of dissent or jokes on Twitter, and "trigger warnings" to avoid emotionally upsetting ideas. Appropriating visceral language from legitimate mental illnesses seems to be the norm, to associate themselves with this abnormally high emotional state. These are who I consider to be NeoRomantics, in that they seem living charicatures of the artistic romance genre.

It is difficult to discuss NeoRomanticism rationally because, by nature, it embodies the idea that reason is an evil to the human condition. I must again be clear that embodying this sentiment differs entirely from the romantics, because these are charicatures and not people who produce works in literature, philosophy, etc. While we may argue their actions irrational, in embodying the belief that only feelings matter, if ONLY THEIR FEELINGS MATTER it is impossible to have such a discussion. While many NeoRomantics participate in online crusades against harrassment, for example, the specific type of "harrassment" they are crusading against tends to be ideological disagreement. For while they harrass people themselves, what's truly going on is they demand an emotional "safe space" where your views are all considered legitimate instead of rationally challenged. When you rationally challenge them, they shout you down, block you, or get you banned, because you aren't playing along with the emotionally-safe playing field of "all arguments are equally valid".

Additionally, you will note the visceral terminology involved in neoromantic apologies. Neoromantics will use visceral terminology, such as "Warrior" in Social Justice Warrior, or claim "harrassment", or re-define words like "rape" to cover as broad a meaning as possible. Acting as living embodiments of romance-era ideals of emotional or childlike behavior, they find themselves generally driven to appropriate as many visceral terms as they can. Again, I clarify, they embody the CONSEQUENCES of ideals of the romance era, and are not themselves romantics.

This is further evidenced, I believe, by the tendency of NeoRomantics to rewrite history. The rewriting of history to hero-worship perspectives (Thomas Carlyle), is revitalized in the groups I have labeled NeoRomantics. For they also endeavor to produce their own versions of history, and replace critical analysis of academic historians with the idealistic stories of heroes and villains. While this has not extended to nationalism in the fashion of the Romance era, it has resulted in a similar effect on ideology. For the ideology of these groups are generally quite hegemonic, and recount histories as though their ideology is the hero and all others the villain, while disregarding any factual basis for the narratives presented. Which was a general problem in the Historiography of Romanticism, in that it presented itself as a narrative instead of the disjointed facts it tends to be.
